parameters.label: Signal strength
parameters.help: Antenna signal level. Lowering it brings snow first, then flickering and lost colour as the colour burst drowns, then broken sync as the sync pulses do — the order a real set fails in.

parameters.label: Vertical hold
parameters.help: The vertical oscillator's free-running speed. Near the centre the sync pulses pull it into lock; past the lock range the picture rolls, with the blanking bar crossing the screen.

parameters.label: Horizontal hold
parameters.help: The horizontal oscillator's free-running speed. Off centre the picture slides sideways as the AFC strains to hold it; further and lock breaks — the picture tears into diagonal bands and the colour goes wild.

parameters.label: AFC response
parameters.help: How quickly the TV's horizontal AFC follows timing changes. Slow sets ride out noise but bend at the top of the picture on VCR playback (flagging); fast ones track tape timing but jitter in noise.

parameters.label: Brightness
parameters.help: Raises the picture tube's black level, as turning up a TV's brightness did. The blanking intervals and sync pulses become visible when the picture rolls or tears.

parameters.label: Ghost
parameters.help: A reflected copy of the signal arriving late (multipath). Negative values invert it, as reflections often did. Its colour shifts with the delay, because the delayed colour carrier arrives at a different phase.

parameters.label: Ghost delay
parameters.help: How late the reflection arrives. 1 µs is about 2% of the picture width — a reflection path roughly 300 m longer than the direct one.

parameters.label: Hum
parameters.help: Mains hum leaking into the video: light and dark bars that drift slowly up the picture (60 Hz hum against the 59.94 Hz colour field rate), bending the picture where the sync separator is pulled off.

parameters.label: Caption data
parameters.help: Line 21 carries closed-caption data — the row of dashes visible in the blanking bar when the picture rolls.

parameters.label: Head switching
parameters.help: Timing jump when the VCR changes heads, just before vertical sync. The bottom lines jump sideways and the TV's AFC chases the jump into the top of the next field — the bend called flagging.

parameters.label: Time-base jitter
parameters.help: Tape stretch and transport flutter. The TV's AFC follows the slow wander; the fast jitter shows as ragged lines.

parameters.label: Tape crinkle
parameters.help: Creased tape passing the heads: bands of signal loss and violent timing errors, enough to knock the TV out of lock for a moment.

parameters.label: Head clog
parameters.help: Debris on the video heads, lifting them off the tape: whole fields drop out to noise and lose their sync, more often as the clog worsens.

parameters.label: Tracking error
parameters.help: The heads drifting off the recorded tracks. Well tracked, the noise band where they cross to the next track rests in the vertical interval, out of sight; as the error grows it climbs into the picture and widens.

parameters.label: Search
parameters.help: Fast-forward picture search. The spinning heads cross from track to track, reading noise between them: one fewer noise bar than the speed, drifting as the tracking phase slides, with the picture jumping at each crossing.

parameters.label: Dropouts
parameters.help: Oxide missing from the tape: brief losses of signal, often a few lines tall. How they look depends on Dropout compensation.

parameters.label: Dropout compensation
parameters.help: The VCR's fix for dropouts: replay the lost stretch from the line before. On, dropouts shrink to brief white ticks and short smears where one line repeats down a tall flaw; off, they show as long white streaks.
